# Mary Vance

## Overview

- **Status:** alive  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER IX. UNA INTERVENES P44](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0044)</sub>

## Appearance

Mary Vance has a plump face with rosy cheeks and elaborately crimped hair. Her distinct, white, queer-looking eyes shine, though they have also been described as looking like burnt holes in a blanket after she has cried.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XVIII. MARY BRINGS EVIL TIDINGS P5](../source/v05-c18.md#nw-v05-c18-p0005), [v5 CHAPTER XXXI. CARL DOES PENANCE P28](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0028)_

## Personality

Mary Vance is generally a jolly, agreeable, and stimulating companion who is loyal to her friends. Though she is described as a sly child and silly regarding certain mistaken beliefs, she is not overly sensitive, except on specific points where she exhibits a temper. She often speaks with brutal frankness, frequently enters a lecturing mood, and holds pessimistic views about stepmothers. A remarkably hardworking individual who excels at labor, she is skilled in cooking, can read, write, and cipher up to fractions, and possesses talent for playing the jew's-harp and making shadow pictures with her fingers. Additionally, she harbors a fear of ghosts.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P87](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0087), [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P14](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0014), [v5 CHAPTER VI. ## History

Mary Vance, a runaway orphan who had been abused by her former guardian Mrs. [Wiley](../character/wiley.md), was found starving in a barn loft by the Meredith children. They brought her to the manse, where she was fed, given clean clothes, and accommodated in the garret. She quickly settled into life at the manse, taking over housecleaning duties and spending time with the local children in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley). After learning that Mrs. [Wiley](../character/wiley.md) had died, Mary was adopted by [Cornelia Bryant](../character/cornelia-bryant.md) upon [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) Meredith's intervention. Settling into her new home, Mary often shared neighborhood gossip, warnings, and stories with the Meredith and [Blythe](../character/blythe.md) children, while boasting of her upgraded wardrobe. On various occasions, she warned [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) about the prospect of her father remarrying, informed [Faith](../character/faith.md) about threats to Mr. Meredith's pastoral position, and lectured the children on how their wild behavior caused public scandal.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P4](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0004), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P14](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0014), [v5 CHAPTER V. ## Quotes

> "You think you’re something, don’t you, all dressed up like a doll! Look at me. My dress is all rags and I don’t care! I’d rather be ragged than a doll baby. Go home and tell them to put you in a glass case. Look at me—look at me—look at me!"
>
> — Mary Vance — [v5 CHAPTER VII. A FISHY EPISODE P9](../source/v05-c07.md#nw-v05-c07-p0009)

> “That yarn about the divining rod is no lie, anyhow,” said Mary. “Old Jake Crawford over-harbour can work it. They send for him from everywhere when they want to dig a well. And I believe I know the Wandering Jew.”
>
> — Mary Vance — [v5 CHAPTER VIII. MISS CORNELIA INTERVENES P17](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0017)

> "That slipped out ‘fore I thought—it did, honest to—I mean, true’s you live, and I swallowed half of it. You folks over here are mighty squeamish seems to me. Wish you could have heard the Wileys when they had a fight."
>
> — Mary Vance — [v5 CHAPTER VIII. MISS CORNELIA INTERVENES P32](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0032)

> “I ain’t a lady,” said Mary. “What chance’ve I ever had of being a lady? But I won’t say that again if I can help it. I promise you.”
>
> — Mary Vance — [v5 CHAPTER VIII. MISS CORNELIA INTERVENES P35](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0035)

> “I don’t expect Him to answer ‘em anyhow,” said Mary of little faith. “I’ve been asking Him for a week to clear up this Wiley affair and He hasn’t done a thing. I’m going to give up.”
>
> — Mary Vance — [v5 CHAPTER VIII. MISS CORNELIA INTERVENES P37](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0037)

## Relationships

### [Carl](../character/carl.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/carl--mary-vance.md)

[Carl](../character/carl.md) is one of the children Mary Vance bonds with after she is taken in by the Meredith family as a runaway orphan. Their friendship includes spending time together in the graveyard, where they observed ants. Mary also interacts with him alongside the other children in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley), joining in their discussions and sharing stories.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P4](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0004), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P14](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0014), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P27](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0027), +10 more_

### [Faith](../character/faith.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/faith--mary-vance.md)

Mary Vance and [Faith](../character/faith.md) share a friendship marked by companionship and occasional friction. After [Faith](../character/faith.md) and her siblings find the runaway Mary hiding in a barn, [Faith](../character/faith.md) lends her clean clothes and helps arrange a place for her to sleep. Though they enjoy walking together and spending time in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley), Mary occasionally clashes with [Faith](../character/faith.md) over local gossip and antics.

### [Jem](../character/jem.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/jem--mary-vance.md)

[Jem](../character/jem.md) is Mary Vance's favorite among the local children. She frequently spends time with him and the group in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley) and around the manse. Even as Mary occasionally scolds the Meredith children about their behavior, [Jem](../character/jem.md) remains a respected presence who offers constructive advice to the group.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P8](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0008), [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P15](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0015), [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P19](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0019), +14 more_

### [Una Meredith](../character/una-meredith.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/mary-vance--una-meredith.md)

[Una Meredith](../character/una-meredith.md) is a close playmate and supportive friend to Mary Vance, comforting her when she cries over her past abusive guardian and bravely convincing Miss Cornelia to adopt her. Mary acts as a mentor to [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) by teaching her how to wash dishes and taking over household cleaning tasks at the manse. Their relationship features deep personal conversations, though Mary occasionally causes [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) distress by sharing blunt warnings about potential stepmothers.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P4](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0004), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P14](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0014), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P27](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0027), +24 more_
